content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Rule T4C is satisfied at the **preferred** position:

| Rule element | Document | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | §9.4 — Agreement or any Order Form, without cause | ✅ Preferred |
| Notice period | §29.4 — thirty days | ✅ Preferred (30 days) |
| Early-termination fee | Only accrued Fees; no penalty | ✅ Better than fallback |
| Refund of prepaid fees | §9.4 + §10.2 | ✅ Preferred |
| Vendor convenience right | None exists | ✅ Preferred |

The three-year term in §8.1 made the Customer convenience right essential, and it is present on preferred terms.

Two items noted in the rationale but deliberately **not** flagged as deviations under this rule:

1. **Cross-referenced notice period** — the 30 days sits in §29.4 rather than in §9.4 itself. Substantively correct, merely awkward placement.
2. **Defective "Fees" definition (§1.5)** — "Fees" is defined as *only* the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, which conflicts with its use in §§7.1, 8.3 and 10.2 and, read literally, would shrink the §9.4 refund to the implementation charge. This is a document-wide definitional defect touching fees, refunds and any fee-based liability cap, so it belongs to a definitions/fees rule rather than being recharacterized as a termination-for-convenience deviation — this rule's material terms all sit at or above preferred.

I also declined to flag §7.7 (15%-per-week late-payment liquidated damages) here; it is a payment-terms problem, not a convenience-termination penalty, and flagging it under T4C would double-count it. It is worth raising under the payment/penalty rule, as it is aggressive.
